Author: Tristan Towns, Lacey Howard

Summary: Empower children to embrace self-acceptance, empathy, and positive affirmations with " I Am Me ," a must-have for any home or school social-emotional library. This uplifting and vibrant story invites children to embrace their uniqueness and celebrate the diversity around them, fostering a deep sense of inclusion and understanding. "I Am Me" delights with its fun rhymes and colorful illustrations, guiding children on a journey of self-discovery and acceptance. Through powerful affirmations and relatable characters of various ethnic backgrounds, abilities, and appearances-including those with glasses, freckles, different hair colors, and a character using a wheelchair-this book encourages children to embrace their own identity while appreciating the differences in others. From characters with autism and Down syndrome to those with prosthetic arms and vitiligo, "I Am Me" showcases the beauty of diversity in all its forms. Each character's unique traits are celebrated, teaching children the importance of empathy and acceptance toward individuals with different abilities and special needs. With each turn of the page, children are inspired to practice self-love through positive self-talk and to extend kindness and understanding to everyone they encounter. " I Am Me " instills confidence in children to embrace who they are while fostering a deep appreciation for the value of diversity. Whether read at home or in the classroom, " I Am Me " is a valuable resource for parents, teachers, and caregivers seeking to instill important social-emotional skills and nurture a culture of acceptance and respect for all. Its engaging narrative and diverse characters make it a wonderful tool for sparking meaningful conversations about self-acceptance, empathy, and diversity. Perfect for teaching valuable life lessons such as:  Building self-confidenceSpreading kindnessNurturing self-loveEmbracing diversity

Jamerson is a little boy who wants to make friends, but he just finds sharing his thoughts so hard! So he turns to what he knows best...mixing and baking to relieve his stress. Words for Sale teaches children the importance of having empathy and accepting friends that may be different.

Categories (Amazon): Books > Children's Books > Growing Up & Facts of Life > Difficult Discussions > Prejudice & Racism
Summary: Not So Different is a children's picture book that encourages young readers to celebrate diversity and embrace inclusion. The story spotlights a biracial main character who is learning to understand his family's unique interracial dynamic and navigate friendships within a diverse community.  Throughout the narrative, he recognizes the importance of our distinct individual characteristics and what they bring to the group, as well as the ways in which we are really all the same. While playful and lighthearted, Not So Different is a wonderful tool that can be used to start necessary difficult conversations with our children about race, diversity, racism, bullying, and inclusion.  Written for readers from ages 1-10, this children's book can be understood on many levels by young readers of all ages. Babies and toddlers will enjoy the bold, colorful pictures and quick poetic pace, while school-aged children will be able to sympathize with the main character's deeper experiences relating to self-esteem, self-respect, and respect for others.
